Run a full decomposition analysis

Source: R/decompose.R
shapley_decompose.Rd

This is the main user-facing function. Given a model object that implements the shapleydecomp S3 interface, it performs a complete factorial decomposition of the specified factors across all decomposition years.

Usage

shapley_decompose(
  model,
  params,
  factors,
  summary_vars,
  decomp_years,
  method = "shapley",
  cf_type = CF_CHANGE_SINCE,
  baseline_year = min(decomp_years),
  extended = TRUE,
  step_scenarios = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  n_cores = 1L,
  group_vars = character(),
  ...
)

Arguments

model

An S3 model object. Must have methods for run_simulation(), summarize_results(), build_counterfactual(), and get_baseline_value().

params

Model parameters (model-specific list/object).

factors

Character vector of factor names to decompose.

summary_vars

Character vector of summary variable names (columns in the output of summarize_results()).

decomp_years

Integer vector of years at which to perform decomposition (e.g., 2000:2023).

method

Character, decomposition method. Only "shapley" (default) is supported. "das_gupta" is accepted as a deprecated alias: Das Gupta's symmetric standardization is the special case of the Shapley value for binary on/off factors, so the weights are identical.

cf_type

Character, counterfactual type: "change_since" (default) — counterfactual is the value at the baseline year; or "total_impact" — counterfactual is zero / no intervention.

baseline_year

Integer, the reference year for "change_since" counterfactuals. Defaults to min(decomp_years).

extended

Logical, whether to compute the extended factor decomposition (effects at all output years >= decomp year). Default TRUE.

step_scenarios

Logical, whether to compute step scenarios (all-on time series per decomp year). Default TRUE.

verbose

Logical, print progress messages. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer, number of cores for parallel counterfactual simulation runs. Default 1 (sequential). Values > 1 run every counterfactual simulation, across all decomp years, in one parallel::mclapply() map, so that more cores than the 2^n runs of a single year can be used. Windows does not support forking, so there it falls back to sequential with a warning.

group_vars

Character vector of columns in the output of summarize_results() that identify independent groups, such as locations or draws, each decomposed separately. Default none.

...

Additional arguments passed to model methods.

Value

A list with components:

decomp

data.table — standard year-by-year decomposition (one row per decomp year × measure, factor effects in columns)

step_scenarios

data.table — all-on time series per decomp year (columns: step_year, year, plus summary vars). NULL if step_scenarios = FALSE.

extended_decomp

data.table — extended decomposition (factor effects at all years >= decomp year). NULL if extended = FALSE.

run_table

data.table — the factorial design table used.

run_summary

data.table — per decomp year: the number of coalition runs, how many were simulated, how many were reused from the previous step, and the factors that were null players (their counterfactual left the params unchanged, so their effect is 0).

params

List of decomposition parameters used.

Details

The decomposition is sequential (Carter 2025, Quantifying averted burden from infectious disease control policies, PhD dissertation, University of Washington, https://hdl.handle.net/1773/53310). At each decomp year y, every policy before y is at its observed value, every policy after y is at its counterfactual, and only the year-y policy varies across the 2^n coalitions. The attribution at step y is therefore the marginal impact of the year-y policy, conditional on the past and undiluted by the future. extended_decomp records that impact at every later year, and sequential_totals() sums the steps into each factor's total impact at every year.

See also

vignette("shapleydecomp") for a worked example, and validate_model_interface to check a model first.

Examples

# A two-factor SIR model shipped with the package
sir <- new.env()
sys.source(system.file("examples", "sir_model.R", package = "shapleydecomp"),
           envir = sir)
model  <- sir$create_sir_model(years = 1990:2010)
params <- sir$create_sir_params(years = 1990:2010)

res <- shapley_decompose(
  model, params,
  factors      = c("beta_reduction", "treatment_effect"),
  summary_vars = c("infections", "deaths"),
  decomp_years = 2000:2010,
  cf_type      = "total_impact",
  verbose      = FALSE
)
res$decomp
#>     decomp_year    measure beta_reduction treatment_effect

# Each factor's total impact at every year
sequential_totals(res)
